title: Alignment playbook: Product + Eng + Applied ML sync (prep + actions)
content:
Context / why I care (TL;DR):
- Quick sync prepping for cross-functional roadmap alignment meeting (Product + Eng + Applied ML). Goal: make the next 8 weeks’ roadmap decisions explicit for serving runtime changes, model rollout experiments, and evaluation gating so we avoid last-minute rework.
- This doc = my scratchpad for the 1:1 syncs I want to run before the larger forum + the raw notes I expect to capture in-meeting. Rough, abbreviated, actionable.

Meeting objectives (what I want to leave with):
1) Shared, prioritized list (top 3) of customer-impacting items that require infra/runtime changes vs model-only experiments.
2) Agreement on gating criteria for any model swap in hosted API (quality eval thresholds, latency bump tolerance, cost delta cap).
3) Clear owners + timelines for two high-risk items: KV cache eviction policy change (runtime) and RLHF inference test harness (applied-ml).
4) One concrete follow-up: schedule a 90-min tech deep-dive with runtime + applied-ml + infra by 2026-03-30.

Pre-read I want people to scan (include links in invite):
- short explainer: GH-PR-789 (routing + kernel selection changes) — runtime perf tradeoffs, short notes.
- Confluence: INFER-ROADMAP-Q2-2026 — current draft roadmap.
- Eval brief: rl-feedback-harness-v2 (applied-ml notebook summary).

Background notes / where we are now (my understanding):
- Product: pushing two initiatives as customers ask: (A) lower-cost short-chat SKU (quantized model + aggressive batching), (B) higher-quality long-context SKU (larger model + persistent KV caching).
- Eng/Serving runtime: kernel selector refactor planned in April; risk: temporary latency jitter for some shapes. KV cache eviction is conservative now — causes slightly higher mem pressure but fewer cache misses.
- Applied ML: new RLHF inference harness ready but not integrated with our staging traffic; metrics to check: reward-model delta, hallucination rate (as measured by syntactic/semantic eval set), sampling stability across seeds.

Key tradeoffs to surface in the sync (short bullets):
- Latency vs Cost vs Quality: short-chat SKU reduces cost but may increase response diversity (sampling artifacts) — Product wants cost wins >10% for customers to justify.
- Rollout risk: switching routing to prefer quantized variants may expose regional perf regressions; need canary plan that includes region + model-version + quantization combo.
- Eval gating: applied-ml wants a 95% pass on core prompt set; Eng wants a lighter-weight smoke check to avoid blocking deploys. Need a reconciliation.

Suggested agenda (30–45 min):
- 0–5m: Quick context + priorities (me)
- 5–15m: Product states use-cases and target KPIs (Maya) — what customers asked, OKR ties
- 15–25m: Applied ML share: RLHF harness outputs & gating proposal (Aisha)
- 25–35m: Eng / runtime impact: kernel + KV eviction + rollout plan (Dmitri)
- 35–45m: Decide top-3 actionable items, owners, and next steps; confirm 90-min deep-dive time slot

Notes to raise (conversation starters):
- "If we relax KV eviction one notch, what worst-case RAM bump do we see on p3.xlarge?" (ask Dmitri)
- "Can applied-ml provide a 10-min smoke harness that runs <5% of the full eval but correlates with the full metric?" (ask Aisha)
- "Product: is 10% cost reduction the threshold customers care about, or is the decision more about availability & SLAs?" (ask Maya)

Potential decisions I want on record:
- Approve a canary matrix: 5% traffic in region-us-west with quantized model + throttle to 50 rps per instance for 48 hours.
- Use applied-ml's smoke harness as pre-deploy gate; full eval runs asynchronously and must pass within 24 hours of canary start or auto-rollback.
- Postpone any global kernel selector refactor rollout until after the 90-min deep-dive unless we can prove zero-latency-regressions on a staging workload.

Open questions / unknowns (for follow-up):
- Who will own the smoke harness integration end-to-end? (applied-ml to own metrics, Eng to own CI run) — still need a named owner + ticket.
- Is there an agreed metric for "hallucination rate" that Product signs off on? (Aisha -> propose a short list by 2026-03-24)
- Edge case: if canary shows regional >10% latency spike but no quality regression, do we pause or throttle? Need policy.

Draft action items (captured as shorthand; will convert to JIRA after meeting):
- AI-1: Create JIRA ticket for "smoke-harness-integration" with checklist: artifact, CI job, pre-deploy hook, alerting. Owner: Aisha. Due: 2026-03-27.
- AI-2: Run memory delta simulation for KV eviction change on p3.xlarge and provide numbers (peak mem, 95th lat) Owner: Dmitri. Due: 2026-03-24.
- AI-3: Product to confirm cost-win threshold + customer examples (Maya). Due: 2026-03-23.
- AI-4: I (Ryan) to book 90-min deep-dive and prepare short tech scope doc. Due: 2026-03-25.
- AI-5: Applied-ML to produce candidate pass/fail thresholds for the core prompt set (list of 10 prompts + numeric thresholds). Owner: Aisha. Due: 2026-03-24.
- AI-6: Eng to draft canary matrix + rollback criteria and post it to Confluence. Owner: Dmitri. Due: 2026-03-22.

Notes-from-1:1s I want to run before sync (quick bullets):
- 1:1 with Maya (Product) — confirm top customer asks, hear if any legal/compliance constraints for long-context SKU.
- 1:1 with Aisha (Applied ML) — clarify what the RLHF harness measures and which metrics are brittle.
- 1:1 with Dmitri (Eng) — get a concrete perf risk doc for kernel selector change.

Things I'm worried about (biases / assumptions):
- I may be overweighting cost wins because infra is noisy this quarter; need to ensure Product still values quality for the long-context SKU.
- Applied-ML's full eval takes too long; we must avoid a gating policy that stalls deploys.
- We need a safe, minimal rollback path; otherwise canaries are risky.

Meeting checklist (quick):
- Invite includes links (PR, Confluence, eval summary) — done? check before sending.
- Confirm Aisha + Dmitri + Maya can share 3 slides max each.
- Bring the short decision template (matrix: option / risk / owner / timeframe).

Post-meeting capture plan (my note-to-self):
- Immediately after meeting: update JIRA tickets for AIs, paste concise meeting notes into Confluence section INFER-ROADMAP-Q2-2026/meeting-notes with the canary matrix.
- If there is any decision that changes SLAs, loop in SRE and Legal through email + cc.

Rough script lines (useful for steering):
- "We need 3 explicit wins we can ship in 8 weeks that don't expand scope. Let's pick the smallest ship that yields measurable customer impact."
- "If applied-ml's full eval is slow, agree on a lightweight smoke that correlates, then tighten post-canary."

Final: my immediate next steps before the sync (today):
- DM Maya to confirm she can present the customer examples (done: note left).
- Draft the canary matrix skeleton and attach to meeting invite (in progress).
- Ping Aisha for quick note on smoke harness dimension (waiting on reply).

Random scratch / to self:
- Think about adding a "regression budget" concept (X latency ms and Y quality delta) to make decisions more objective.
- Consider small experiment: route 1% traffic to quantized model for 24h overnight to collect telemetry without formal canary. Might be easier for Product to greenlight.

-- end of scratchpad --

(Will tidy and convert to proper meeting notes & JIRA tasks after the sync; this is intentionally messy so I can capture quick thoughts in real time.)
